The market's leadership has changed. Many of the mega-ap growth stocks that drove the indexes to new heights in recent years are now lagging.

The Nasdaq-100, which is the 100 largest non-financial stocks in the Nasdaq Composite (NASDAQINDEX: ^IXIC), is up 12.4% year-to-date (YTD) at the time of this writing. Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA), Microsoft (NASDAQ: MSFT), and Amazon (NASDAQ: AMZN) have produced smaller gains, while Meta Platforms (NASDAQ: META), Alphabet (NASDAQ: GOOG) (NASDAQ: GOOGL), and Tesla (NASDAQ: TSLA) are down YTD. This means that six "Magnificent Seven" stocks are underperforming the Nasdaq-100 YTD -- the only exception being Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL).

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Here's why the Vanguard Morningstar Mega Cap Growth ETF (NYSEMKT: MGK) is an excellent low-cost way to buy the dip on top growth stocks.

Image source: Getty Images.
The Mega Cap Growth ETF has 67.6% in 10 stocks

The Mega Cap Growth ETF is essentially a more concentrated version of the Vanguard Morningstar Growth ETF (NYSEMKT: VUG). The Mega Cap ETF has 52 holdings compared to 135 for the Growth ETF. The expense ratio of the Mega Cap ETF is 0.05% -- only slightly higher than the Growth ETF's 0.03% expense ratio. It's worth noting that 0.03% is the lowest you'll find for any ETF. The largest ETF by net assets in the world is the Vanguard S&P 500 ETF, which also has a 0.03% expense ratio.

AAPL data by YCharts

Because of the sheer size of the largest U.S. companies, the top 10 holdings in the Mega Cap Growth ETF make up a staggering 67.6% of the fund -- including a combined 44.4% in the six "Magnificent Seven" stocks that are underperforming the Nasdaq-100 YTD.

Investing in leading Nasdaq and NYSE growth stocks

The Mega Cap Growth ETF is a great buy for investors who believe today's most valuable companies will continue leading the broader market over the long term. But some investors may lean toward buying a Nasdaq-100 index ETF, such as the popular Invesco QQQ Trust (NASDAQ: QQQ), rather than the Mega Cap Growth ETF. The issue with that strategy is twofold.

For starters, the Invesco QQQ Trust has a relatively high expense ratio of 0.18%. And, more importantly, it invests exclusively in Nasdaq-listed non-financial companies -- meaning it excludes key growth stocks listed on the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE).

title: Alphabet, Amazon, and Microsoft All Surged Today. You Can Thank the Big Blue Wave.
detail:
Alphabet, Amazon, and Microsoft All Surged Today. You Can Thank the Big Blue Wave.
Danny Vena, CPA, The Motley Fool
Wed, November 4, 2026 at 1:45 PM MST 5 min read
GOOG
AMZN
MSFT
NVDA
^DJI
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

With the 2026 election in the books, early signs Wednesday point to a positive day for investors, with the three major market indexes pushing higher. The price-weighted Dow Jones Industrial Average is up 3% (as of this writing), the broad-based S&P 500 has gained 1.7%, and the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite is up 1.7%.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Helping lead the major indexes higher are the "Big Three" cloud providers, Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN), Microsoft (NASDAQ:MSFT), and Alphabet (NASDAQ:GOOGL) (NASDAQ:GOOG), gaining 7.1%, 7%, and 4.1%, respectively, as I write this.

Given the expected shift in the regulatory environment, it might seem counterintuitive that these tech titans would gain ground, but dig a little deeper, and it's easy to see why shareholders are optimistic.

Image source: Getty Images.

Democrats win control of Congress

Democrats have won control of both the House and Senate, and some won high-profile gubernatorial races. Many market watchers expect the Blue Wave to lead to tighter controls and stricter regulations for data centers. The proliferation of artificial intelligence (AI) has sparked a data center boom, with spending projected to reach as much as $5.2 trillion by 2030, according to global management consulting firm McKinsey & Company.

That build-out could come to a screeching halt in the wake of the Blue Wave. Many Democrats campaigned on platforms seeking moratoriums on data center construction. Texas, Ohio, Georgia, and Arizona are the top locations for data center capacity coming online in 2028, with Texas accounting for 41% of new construction. Democratic governor-elect Gina Hinojosa of Texas supports a moratorium until the legislature can assess the impact on power, water, and other local resources.

It wasn't just Democrats. There were an estimated 50 data center-related ballot measures across 10 states, with many seeking to ban new construction or enact strict controls. Many are expected to pass once the final ballot count is complete.

Given the prevailing headwinds, why are the hyperscalers rising today? Amazon, Microsoft, and Alphabet dominate the data center space, accounting for more than half the top 15 data centers by capacity in North America, according to analysis conducted by Axios. Any move to limit new data center construction would increase their dominance by limiting new competition.

Microsoft's shares have outperformed the Zacks Computer - Software industry over the year-to-date period (+15.3% vs. -1.1%). The company is benefiting from accelerating Azure demand, with Azure revenue jumping 48% to $33.2 billion in first-quarter fiscal 2027 and guidance calling for 49-50% constant-currency growth in the second quarter. 

AI monetization is broadening across Microsoft 365 Copilot, GitHub Copilot and Foundry, where revenues more than tripled. Commercial remaining performance obligation of $677 billion, up 73%, provides strong revenue visibility. Microsoft 365 commercial cloud growth is being driven by ARPU gains from premium E5, E7 and Copilot offerings.

Shares of SpaceX have gained +2.4% over the year-to-date period against the Zacks Wireless National industry's gain of +119.4%. The company launch franchise, expanding Starlink network and growing Super Intelligence operations offer long-term potential. Starship's orbital satellite deployment improves the outlook for network capacity and launch efficiency. 

Starlink's recurring revenues and rising enterprise adoption add an established earnings base. New cloud contracts and Cursor strengthen AI monetization, while integrated engineering may lower deployment costs. 

However, the rapid compute buildout demands substantial capital and exposes returns to power, equipment and customer utilization risks. Starship reuse and mobile network expansion remain costly and complex. Despite better quarterly profitability, sustained cash generation and returns on new assets remain unproven. The balance of growth prospects and execution risks supports a Neutral view.

(You can read the full research report on SpaceX here >>>)

Marvell's shares have outperformed the Zacks Electronics - Semiconductors industry over the year-to-date period (+92% vs. +11.8%). The company is benefiting from rising AI infrastructure demand, with custom silicon, interconnect, switching and optics supporting record data center revenues and a higher multi-year outlook. 

Management now expects faster growth through fiscal 2028 as custom programs broaden and scale-up networking gains traction. The NVIDIA relationship and recent acquisitions expand Marvell's role across next-generation AI architectures, while the Communications and Other segment provides some diversification. 

Offsetting these positives, the custom ramp-up is expected to weigh on gross margin, and revenues are becoming more concentrated in data center and large customers. Supply constraints, export controls and tariffs can disrupt execution, while intense competition and uneven communications demand add volatility. These factors support a balanced view. 

(You can read the full research report on Marvell here >>>)

Shares of Preformed Line Products have outperformed the Zacks Electronics - Miscellaneous Products industry over the year-to-date period (+46% vs. +15%). This microcap company with a market capitalization of $1.52 billion benefits from grid modernization spending, with strong energy infrastructure demand supporting its core business. Expanding communications capabilities, targeted acquisitions and international manufacturing investments broaden its market reach and growth potential. 

Favorable product mix, pricing actions and operating leverage strengthen profitability. However, tariffs, volatile raw material and freight costs could constrain margins, while rising operating expenses increase dependence on sustained demand. 

Heavy capital spending and expansion initiatives heighten execution risks. Tax fluctuations and foreign exchange movements may also create earnings volatility. Overall, PLPC offers exposure to essential infrastructure investment, but cost discipline and returns on expansion remain critical to its investment appeal.

title: IREN Fell 4% on Cipher’s Miss, Then Jumped 10%. Here’s What Its November 5 Report Has to Settle

Trading disclosure
IREN Fell 4% on Cipher's Miss, Then Jumped 10%. Here's What Its November 5 Report Has to Settle ©SUMALI IBNU CHAMID from Alemedia.id, Brett Sayles from Pexels via Canva
Key Takeaways

IREN fell 4% on Nov. 2 after Cipher Digital missed revenue estimates, then jumped 10% the next morning as AI data center stocks rebounded.

On its call, Cipher said change orders and higher construction costs would have cut its yield on cost to about 13% from roughly 15% if it hadn't renegotiated its lease.

IREN plans $25 billion to $30 billion of capex this fiscal year, and much of it is GPUs from Dell for its Microsoft contract. It has already said new deployments will cost 15% to 20% more.

IREN can handle higher costs as long as lenders and customers keep paying for most of the build, so the funding gap and the share count matter most in Thursday's report.

IREN (IREN:NASDAQ) fell 4% on Monday after Cipher Digital (CIFR:NASDAQ) missed revenue estimates. Then it jumped 10% on Tuesday morning as AI data center stocks bounced back.

For IREN, the most important number in Cipher's report is a cost. IREN reports its fiscal first quarter on Thursday, Nov. 5, after the close, and its own build is far bigger. Two companies have a stake in the results. Microsoft (MSFT:NASDAQ) signed the $9.7 billion, five-year contract at the center of IREN's AI cloud. Dell Technologies (DELL:NYSE) sells IREN the GPUs that contract runs on.

TIKR tracks 20 analysts on IREN. How many say "Buy"?

See the full breakdown of Buy, Hold, and Sell ratings on IREN, along with Wall Street's revenue and earnings estimates, all in one place. More than 500,000 investors use TIKR to research stocks like this one. See IREN's Analyst Ratings

Cipher's costs ran over

Cipher's third-quarter revenue was $26.7 million, short of estimates because its bitcoin mining revenue shrank. Keefe Bruyette cut its price targets across the group the same day.

The bigger news came on the call. At Cipher's Barber Lake campus, the tenant changed its requirements during construction, which ran up about $409 million of change orders. Cipher agreed to pay $359 million of that itself in exchange for a 10-year lease extension. Without that deal, Cipher said, the change orders, inflation and rising labor costs would have pushed its cost to $12.3 million per IT megawatt, up from the $10.4 million it financed. Its yield on cost would have fallen to about 13% from roughly 15%.

Management said on the call that when tenants make "very substantial change orders, that has knock-on effects to cost and schedule."

Short seller Jim Chanos replied to an X post quoting the call, and his reply ended: "Hard to believe."

IREN builds for its own cloud, so it pays the whole bill, GPUs included. And it has already said the bill is going up. On its August call, management said it expects data center and GPU costs for new deployments to run 15% to 20% higher this fiscal year.

title: Ironically, the Blue Wave Could Make Hyperscalers “Good Businesses Again” by Forcing Capex Discipline
detail:
Ironically, the Blue Wave Could Make Hyperscalers “Good Businesses Again” by Forcing Capex Discipline
Roxanna Maglangit

GOOG

Ironically, the Blue Wave Could Make Hyperscalers "Good Businesses Again" by Forcing Capex Discipline ©@Bianca Constantinescu's Images via Canva, @Angelo Dee from ภาพของSakorn Sukkasemsakorn via Canva
Key Takeaways

Democrats won control of the House and Senate in Tuesday's midterms, and state results point to more limits on building data centers but fewer outright bans.

Tighter rules that slow the build-out would help Amazon, Alphabet, Meta and Microsoft shareholders, because less capex while capacity stays scarce repairs free cash flow without hurting demand.

Free cash flow needs the repair: Amazon's was a $34.8 billion outflow in the September quarter, and Meta's turned negative.

The companies still set their own budgets, and Alphabet's capex keeps climbing, so the 2027 spending plans due early next year are what to watch.

Democrats won the House and the Senate on Tuesday, and one investor thinks that could be the best news in a while for shareholders of Amazon (AMZN:NASDAQ), Alphabet (GOOG), Meta Platforms (META:NASDAQ) and Microsoft (MSFT:NASDAQ).

That sounds backward. Tighter rules on data centers should mean a slower AI build-out, and AI stocks have been priced for a faster one.

But the investor who posts as BuccoCapital on X thinks the slowdown is good for them: "Dem sweep is bullish AI because everyone spends less on capex and diffusion has time to catch up to the buildout. Labs can't miss on revenue bc they are compute constrained."

Another user pushed back that the market's earnings growth leans on chipmakers like Nvidia and Micron, and he waved that off. On the big cloud spenders, he wrote: "The hypers would be good businesses again."

Ironically, I think he's right.

TIKR tracks 59 analysts on Amazon. How many say "Buy"?

See the full breakdown of Buy, Hold, and Sell ratings on Amazon, along with Wall Street's revenue and earnings estimates, all in one place. More than 500,000 investors use TIKR to research stocks like this one. See Amazon's Analyst Ratings

Incumbents get the edge

Jim Cramer, host of CNBC's Mad Money, went through the state-by-state results on data centers and found "more restrictions being put on building them but fewer outright bans." He thinks that "would seem to favor incumbents PLUS spending within means as opposed to endless buildouts."

That's the setup the four giants should want. They already run the capacity, and new rules make everyone's next site slower to build, theirs included. With capacity that tight, demand holds up: Amazon's management says the capacity it adds is sold as soon as it's installed.

And the market already rewards restraint. On Monday's Mad Money, Cramer pointed out that "the only hyperscalers that did dial back its CapEx plans, Microsoft, saw the best reaction from the market for doing so." (Its stock still fell, he added, just by less than the rest.)
